tasks.short: Program complex robotic systems such as vision systems.

steps.what: Program complex robotic systems, such as vision systems, on the controller.

tasks.design: The robotics technician programs the vision system on the robot controller {OTHER} at the cell. That programming stays with the technician. Survey computing, code checks, and title-block extraction in the group digest cover drafters and mapping technicians, and this statement has no second entry of the program.
tasks.previous_blocker: The program depends on the cell, the part, and the fault in front of the technician, not on one rule for every vision system.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's automate bullets cover survey computing, bills of materials, code checks, test reports, and title-block extraction for drafters and mapping technicians in this group. They do not cover programming a vision system, so this task stays as it is.
tasks.still_hard: A vision program that misreads a part sends the arm to the wrong place.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the cell, the part, and the fault while programming the vision system.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The robotics technician still programs the vision system on the controller.

reach.task: Set the vision task the technician programs on the cell
reach.learn: How the technician programs that vision system for this cell.

evidence.claim: Programming a complex robotic vision system stays with the robotics technician. The group digest covers drafting and survey paperwork, not this programming.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the robotics technician programs the vision system at the cell on the robot controller {OTHER}. No structured feed is added, so there is no new field and no producer. If the vision task cannot be read from a system, the technician still programs it by hand. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether some cells also mail the vision program to an engineer after it is written. That mail is not in this statement.
research_questions: Does this technician only program the vision system on the controller, or also retype that program into a second system?

tasks.short: Train robots to perform tasks, including iterative chemical sample tests.

steps.what: To perform simple or complex tasks on the robot.
Train robots using artificial intelligence software or interactive training techniques.
By designing and carrying out a series of iterative tests of chemical samples.

tasks.design: The robotics technician sets the task, trains the robot with the training software {OTHER} or by interactive technique, and carries out the chemical sample series in person. All three stay with the technician. The software named in the statement is the means already in use, and the group digest does not cover this training.
tasks.previous_blocker: The training depends on this robot, this task, and the sample in front of the technician.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's automate bullets cover survey computing, bills of materials, code checks, test reports, and title-block extraction for drafters and mapping technicians in this group. They do not cover training a robot or running a chemical sample series, so this task stays as it is.
tasks.still_hard: A training run that accepts a bad chemical sample series teaches the robot the wrong test.
tasks.human_edge: Judging each sample and each robot response while training on this cell.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The robotics technician still sets the task, still trains the robot, and still runs the sample series.

reach.task: Define the chemical sample series the robot must run
reach.learn: How the technician trains the robot on that series.

evidence.claim: Training a robot with software or interactive technique, including a chemical sample series, stays with the robotics technician. The group digest covers drafting and survey paperwork, not this training.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the robotics technician trains the robot at the cell with the training software {OTHER} or by interactive technique, and carries out the chemical sample tests in person. No structured feed is added, so there is no new field and no producer. If the training task or the sample series cannot be read from a system, the technician still does it. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether some cells also file the sample series in a lab record after the tests. That filing is not in this statement.
research_questions: Does this technician only train the robot and run the sample series, or also retype the series into a second system?

tasks.short: Maintain inventories of robotic production supplies such as sensors or cables.

steps.what: Maintain inventories of robotic production supplies, such as sensors or cables.

tasks.design: The robotics technician counts sensors and cables in the stores and keeps that inventory. The count stays with the technician. A records app in the group digest covers logs and inspection schedules for other tasks, and this statement has no second entry of the count.
tasks.previous_blocker: The count depends on the sensors and cables actually on the shelf, which the technician has to see.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's automate bullets cover survey computing, bills of materials, code checks, test reports, records apps, and title-block extraction for drafters and mapping technicians in this group. They do not cover counting sensors and cables, so this task stays as it is.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong sensor or cable count stops the cell when the part is not on the shelf.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the sensors and cables and judging which ones the cell can still use.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The robotics technician still counts the sensors and cables and still keeps that inventory.

reach.task: Name the sensors and cables the cell must hold
reach.learn: How the technician keeps that inventory by counting the supplies.

evidence.claim: Keeping an inventory of robotic sensors and cables stays with the robotics technician. The group digest covers drafting and survey paperwork, not this count.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the robotics technician counts sensors and cables in the stores. No structured feed is added, so there is no new field and no producer. If a stores record cannot be read, the technician still counts the supplies. A record that already matches this count is the same act, not a second entry this design removes. Manual fallback is that the person continues as now.
Incremental upkeep is zero. No template, mapping, or list is added.
unknowns: Whether some shops already keep this count in a stores record. This statement does not name a second entry after the count.
research_questions: Does this technician only count the sensors and cables, or also retype that count into a second system?
